Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 93, verse 1–3:

Naming of the surah

• It is called al-Duha (The Morning Hours), because it opens with God's oath by the time of morning brightness (al-Duha).

From the aims of the surah

• God reminds His Prophet ﷺ of the blessings He bestowed upon him in his childhood, youth and old age, and refutes the claim of the polytheists, who alleged that God had forsaken the Prophet ﷺ and come to hate him when the revelation ceased. It also gives him good news of the honours prepared for him in the Hereafter, and commands him to be thankful for these blessings in a fitting manner, such as by caring for orphans and showing mercy to the needy.

[The Tafsir]

God swears by the time of morning brightness (al-Duha), and by it is meant the entire day, and by the night when it becomes still with its creatures and its darkness deepens. God swears by whatever He wills of His creations, but it is not permissible for a created being to swear by other than its Creator, for swearing by other than God is shirk. ﴿Your Lord has not forsaken you, [O Prophet], nor has He hated you﴾ by delaying the revelation from you.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 93, verses 6–8:

﴿Did He not find you an orphan and give you refuge?﴾ Your father died while you were still in your mother's womb, and He sheltered and cared for you.

﴿And He found you unaware, and guided you?﴾ He found you not knowing the Book or the faith, so He taught you what you did not know, and enabled you to do the best of deeds.

﴿And He found you poor, and enriched you?﴾ He brought your provision to you, and made you self-sufficient through contentment and patience.
